title: On the Social Value of Life
Population, Productivity, and Sustainable Consumption
abstract: How does sustainable consumption depend on productivity growth, the size and growth rate of the population, and uncertainty over these growth rates? I address these questions using a model in which productivity and population growth are stochastic and human lives can have (positive or negative) intrinsic social value. I show how sustainable consumption depends on expected rates of productivity and population growth, the volatility of those rates, and the dependence of welfare on population. For plausible parameter values, sustainable consumption is well below the optimal welfare-maximizing level. This raises a question: given its cost, should sustainability be a social objective? (JEL E21, E22, E23, J11, Q01)
abstract_zh: 可持续消费如何取决于生产率增长、人口规模与增长率，以及对这些增长率的不确定性？我通过一个模型来探讨这些问题，在该模型中，生产率和人口增长是随机的，人的生命可以具有（正面或负面的）内在社会价值。我展示了可持续消费如何取决于生产率与人口增长的预期速度、这些速度的波动性，以及福利对人口的依赖程度。在合理的参数取值下，可持续消费远低于使福利最大化的最优水平。这引出了一个问题：考虑到其成本，可持续性是否应当成为一项社会目标？（JEL E21, E22, E23, J11, Q01）

title: A Supply Curve for Forest-Based CO2 Removal
abstract: Forestation is viewed as an important means of removing CO2 from the atmosphere and thereby reducing net CO2 emissions. But how much CO2 can be removed, and at what cost? Focusing on forested and forestable areas in South America, and using spatially disaggregated data, we estimate a supply curve for forest-based atmospheric CO2 removal. The supply curve traces out the marginal cost of removing a metric ton of CO2 as a function of total annual CO2 removal. Each point on the curve corresponds to a specific location, and accounts for land opportunity costs as well as costs of tree planting and maintenance. We show that over a billion tons of CO2 can be removed annually via forestation at a cost below $45 per ton, and about 2.5 billion tons can be removed at a cost below $90 per ton. The supply curve applies to only South America, but with sufficient data could be extended to the entire world.
abstract_zh: 造林被视为从大气中清除二氧化碳，从而减少净二氧化碳排放的重要手段。但究竟能清除多少二氧化碳，成本又是多少？本文聚焦南美洲的森林地区和适宜造林的地区，利用空间分解数据，估算了以森林为基础的大气二氧化碳清除供给曲线。该供给曲线描述了清除一吨二氧化碳的边际成本与每年清除总量之间的函数关系。曲线上的每个点对应一个特定地点，并同时考虑了土地机会成本以及植树和维护的成本。我们表明，通过造林，每年可以以低于每吨45美元的成本清除超过10亿吨二氧化碳，而以低于每吨90美元的成本，可以清除约25亿吨。该供给曲线仅适用于南美洲，但只要有足够的数据，它就可以扩展到全世界。

title: Climate Future: Averting and Adapting to Climate Change
A Simple Rule for Pricing with Limited Knowledge of Demand
Welfare Costs of Catastrophes: Lost Consumption and Lost Lives
What We Know and Don't Know about Climate Change, and Implications for Policy
venue: Environmental and Energy Policy and the Economy
abstract: There is a lot we know about climate change, but there is also a lot we don't know. Even if we knew how much CO2 will be emitted over the coming decades, we wouldn't know how much temperatures will rise as a result. And even if we could predict the extent of warming that will occur, we can say very little about its impact. I explain that we face considerable uncertainty over climate change and its impact, why there is so much uncertainty, and why we will continue to face uncertainty in the near future. I also explain the policy implications of climate change uncertainty. First, the uncertainty (particularly over the possibility of a catastrophic climate outcome) creates insurance value, which pushes us to earlier and stronger actions to reduce CO2 emissions. Second, uncertainty interacts with two kinds of irreversibilities. First, CO2 remains in the atmosphere for centuries, making the environmental damage from CO2 emissions irreversible, pushing us to earlier and stronger actions. Second, reducing CO2 emissions requires sunk costs, i.e., irreversible expenditures, which pushes us away from earlier actions. Both irreversibilities are inherent in climate policy, but the net effect is ambiguous.
abstract_zh: 关于气候变化，我们有很多了解，但也有很多未知。即使我们知道未来几十年会排放多少二氧化碳，我们也不知道由此会导致气温上升多少。而且，即使我们能够预测将会发生的变暖程度，我们对其影响也几乎一无所知。我解释了我们在气候变化及其影响上面临的巨大不确定性，说明了这种不确定性为何如此之大，以及为什么在可预见的未来我们仍将面临不确定性。我还阐述了气候变化不确定性的政策含义。第一，不确定性（尤其是灾难性气候结果的可能性）会产生保险价值，这促使我们更早、更有力地采取行动以减少二氧化碳排放。第二，不确定性与两种不可逆性相互作用。其一，二氧化碳在大气中停留数百年，使得二氧化碳排放造成的环境损害不可逆，这推动我们更早、更有力地采取行动。其二，减少二氧化碳排放需要沉没成本，即不可逆的支出，这又会使我们推迟行动。两种不可逆性都内在于气候政策之中，但其净效应并不确定。

title: COVID-19 and the Welfare Effects of Reducing Contagion
Scarcity, Market Power, and Prices at Slot-Constrained Airports: Evidence from Mexico City
venue: Journal of Transport Economics and Policy

title: The Social Cost of Carbon Revisited
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
abstract: An estimate of the social cost of carbon (SCC) is key to climate policy. But how should we estimate the SCC?A common approach is to use an integrated assessment model (IAM) to simulate time paths for the atmospheric CO2 concentration, its impact on global mean temperature, and the resulting reductions in GDP and consumption.I have argued that IAMs have serious deficiencies that make them poorly suited for this job, but what is the alternative?I present a more transparent approach to estimating an average SCC, which I argue is a more useful guide for policy than the marginal SCC derived from IAMs.I rely on a survey through which I elicit expert opinions regarding (1) the probabilities of alternative economic outcomes of climate change, including extreme outcomes such as a 20% or greater reduction in GDP, but not the particular causes of those outcomes; and (2) the reduction in emissions required to avert an extreme outcome. My estimate of the average SCC is the ratio of the present value of damages from an extreme outcome to the total emission reduction needed to avert such an outcome.I discuss the survey instrument, explain how experts were identified, and present results.I obtain SCC estimates of $200/mt or higher, but the variation across experts is large. Trimming outliers and focusing on experts who expressed a high degree of confidence in their answers yields lower SCCs, $80 to $100/mt.
abstract_zh: 对碳的社会成本（SCC）的估计是气候政策的关键。但我们应当如何估计碳的社会成本？一种常见的做法是使用综合评估模型（IAM）来模拟大气二氧化碳浓度的时间路径、其对全球平均气温的影响，以及由此导致的GDP与消费的减少。我曾论证，综合评估模型存在严重缺陷，使其很不适合承担这一任务，但替代方案是什么呢？我提出了一种更为透明的方法来估计平均碳社会成本，并论证其比综合评估模型推导出的边际碳社会成本更能为政策提供有用指引。我依托一项调查，征集专家意见，内容包括：（1）各种经济结局的概率，包括极端结局，例如GDP下降20%或更多，但不包括导致这些结局的具体原因；以及（2）为避免极端结局所需的排放削减量。我对平均碳社会成本的估计，是极端结局损害的现值与避免该结局所需的总减排量之比。我讨论了调查工具、专家的遴选方式，并呈现了结果。我得到的碳社会成本估计为每公吨200美元或更高，但专家之间的差异很大。剔除异常值并聚焦于那些对其回答表现出高度信心的专家后，得到的碳社会成本较低，为每公吨80至100美元。

title: Microeconomics, Ninth Edition
Tropical Forests, Tipping Points, and the Social Cost of Deforestation
abstract: Recent work has suggested that tropical forest and savanna represent alternative stable states, which are subject to drastic switches at tipping points, in response to changes in rainfall patterns and other drivers. Deforestation cost studies have ignored the likelihood and possible economic impact of a forest-savanna critical transition, therefore underestimating the true social cost of deforestation. We explore the implications of a forest-savanna critical transition and propose an alternative framework for calculating the economic value of a standing tropical forest. Our framework is based on an average incremental cost method, as opposed to currently used marginal cost methods, for the design of optimal land-use policy or payments for ecosystem services. We apply this framework to the calculation of the social cost of deforestation of the Amazon rainforest.
abstract_zh: 近期研究表明，热带森林与热带稀树草原可能是两种替代性的稳定状态，它们会因降雨模式及其他驱动因素的变化而在临界点处发生剧烈转换。以往的毁林成本研究忽视了森林—稀树草原关键转变的可能性及其潜在经济影响，因而低估了毁林的真实社会成本。我们探讨了森林—稀树草原关键转变的含义，并提出了一个计算立木热带森林经济价值的替代框架。我们的框架基于平均增量成本方法，而非目前常用的边际成本方法，用于设计最优土地利用政策或生态系统服务付费。我们将该框架应用于计算亚马逊雨林毁林的社会成本。

title: Coase Lecture - Taxes, Targets, and the Social Cost of Carbon
The Use and Misuse of Models for Climate Policy
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy
abstract: In recent articles I have argued that integrated assessment models (IAMs) have flaws that make them close to useless as tools for policy analysis. IAM-based analyses of climate policy create a perception of knowledge and precision that is illusory and can fool policymakers into thinking that the forecasts the models generate have some kind of scientific legitimacy. However, some economists and climate scientists have claimed that we need to use some kind of model for policy analysis and that IAMs can be structured and used in ways that correct for their shortcomings. For example, it has been argued that although we know very little about key relationships in the model, we can get around this problem by attaching probability distributions to various parameters and then simulating the model using Monte Carlo methods. I argue that this would buy us nothing and that a simpler and more transparent approach to the design of climate change policy is preferable. I briefly outline what such an approach would look like.
abstract_zh: 在近期的文章中，我论证了综合评估模型（IAM）存在缺陷，使其几乎无法作为政策分析的工具。基于综合评估模型的气候政策分析，会制造一种关于知识和精确性的假象，这种假象是虚幻的，可能使政策制定者误以为模型给出的预测具有某种科学合法性。然而，一些经济学家和气候科学家主张，我们需要使用某种模型进行政策分析，而且综合评估模型可以通过某些结构设计和使用方式来弥补其缺陷。例如，有人提出，尽管我们对模型中的关键关系知之甚少，但可以通过为各参数赋予概率分布，然后运用蒙特卡洛方法模拟模型，从而绕过这一问题。我认为，这样做并无益处，而一种更简单、更透明的气候变化政策设计方法更为可取。我简要概述了这种方法的大致面貌。

title: Averting Catastrophes that Kill
The Simple Economics of Commodity Price Speculation
Averting Catastrophes: The Strange Economics of Scylla and Charybdis
Risk and Return in the Design of Environmental Policy
venue: Journal of the Association of Environmental and Resource Economists
abstract: I examine risk/return trade-offs for environmental investments and their implications for policy choice. Consider a policy to reduce carbon emissions. To what extent should the policy objective be a reduction in the expected temperature increase versus a reduction in risk? Using a simple model of a stock externality that evolves stochastically, I examine the “willingness to pay” (WTP) for alternative policies that would reduce expected damages versus the variance of those damages. I compute “iso-WTP” curves (social indifference curves) for combinations of risk and expected return as policy objectives. Given cost estimates for reducing risk and increasing expected returns, one can compute the optimal risk-return mix for a policy, and the policy’s social surplus. I illustrate these results by calibrating the model to data for global warming.
abstract_zh: 我考察了环境投资中的风险—收益权衡，及其对政策选择的含义。以旨在减少碳排放的政策为例。政策目标在多大程度上应当是降低预期的气温升幅，而在多大程度上应当是降低风险？我运用一个关于随机演化存量外部性的简单模型，考察了为降低预期损害与降低损害方差而设计的各类替代政策的“支付意愿”（WTP）。我计算了风险与预期收益组合的“等支付意愿”曲线（社会无差异曲线），以作为政策目标。给定降低风险和提高预期收益的成本估计，就可以计算政策的最优风险—收益组合，以及该政策的社会剩余。我通过将模型校准到全球变暖数据上来说明这些结果。

title: Should Governments Use a Declining Discount Rate in Project Analysis?
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy

title: Climate Change Policy: What Do the Models Tell Us?
abstract: Very little. A plethora of integrated assessment models (IAMs) have been constructed and used to estimate the social cost of carbon (SCC) and evaluate alternative abatement policies. These models have crucial flaws that make them close to useless as tools for policy analysis: certain inputs (e.g., the discount rate) are arbitrary, but have huge effects on the SCC estimates the models produce; the models' descriptions of the impact of climate change are completely ad hoc, with no theoretical or empirical foundation; and the models can tell us nothing about the most important driver of the SCC, the possibility of a catastrophic climate outcome. IAM-based analyses of climate policy create a perception of knowledge and precision, but that perception is illusory and misleading. (JEL C51, Q54, Q58)
abstract_zh: 几乎没有什么。大量综合评估模型（IAM）已经被构建并用于估计碳的社会成本（SCC）并评估不同的减排政策。这些模型存在关键缺陷，使其几乎无法作为政策分析的工具：某些输入（例如贴现率）是任意的，却对模型所产生的碳社会成本估计有巨大影响；模型对气候变化影响的描述完全是临时拼凑的，缺乏理论或经验基础；而且，模型无法告诉我们碳社会成本最重要的驱动因素，即灾难性气候结果的可能性。基于综合评估模型的气候政策分析，制造了一种关于知识和精确性的感觉，但这种感觉是虚幻的、具有误导性的。（JEL C51, Q54, Q58）

title: Determining Benefits and Costs for Future Generations
Pricing Carbon Emissions When We Don't Know the Right Price
The Climate Policy Dilemma
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy
abstract: Climate policy poses a dilemma for environmental economists. The economic argument for stringent greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement is far from clear. There is disagreement among both climate scientists and economists concerning the likelihood of alternative climate outcomes, the nature and extent of the uncertainty of those outcomes, and the framework that should be used to evaluate potential benefits from GHG abatement, including key policy parameters. I argue that the case for stringent abatement—if it can be made at all—cannot be based on the kinds of modeling exercises that have permeated the literature thus far, but instead must be based on the possibility of a catastrophic outcome. I discuss how an analysis that incorporates such an outcome might be conducted.
abstract_zh: 气候政策给环境经济学家带来了一个两难困境。支持严格温室气体减排的经济学论证远不清晰。气候科学家与经济学家之间，对于各种气候结局的可能性、这些结局的不确定性的性质与程度，以及用于评估温室气体减排潜在收益的框架（包括关键政策参数），都存在分歧。我认为，严格减排的理由——如果能够成立的话——不能建立在迄今文献中充斥的那类建模练习之上，而必须建立在灾难性结局的可能性之上。我讨论了如何开展一项纳入此类结局的分析。

title: The Economic and Policy Consequences of Catastrophes
Uncertain Outcomes and Climate Change Policy
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
abstract: Focusing on tail effects, I incorporate distributions for temperature change and its economic impact in an analysis of climate change policy. I estimate the fraction of consumption w*(τ) that society would be willing to sacrifice to ensure that any increase in temperature at a future point is limited to τ. Using information on the distributions for temperature change and economic impact from studies assembled by the IPCC and from “integrated assessment models” (IAMs), I fit displaced gamma distributions for these variables. Unlike existing IAMs, I model economic impact as a relationship between temperature change and the growth rate of GDP as opposed to its level, so that warming has a permanent impact on future GDP. The fitted distributions for temperature change and economic impact generally yield values of w*(τ) below 2%, even for small values of τ, unless one assumes extreme parameter values and/or substantial shifts in the temperature distribution. These results are consistent with moderate abatement policies.
abstract_zh: 我聚焦于尾部效应，将气温变化及其经济影响的分布纳入气候变化政策分析。我估计了社会为确保未来某一时点的气温升幅被限制在τ之内，愿意牺牲的消费比例w*(τ)。利用IPCC汇编的研究以及“综合评估模型”（IAM）中关于气温变化和经济影响的信息，我拟合了这些变量的移位伽马分布。与现有的综合评估模型不同，我将经济影响建模为气温变化与GDP增长率之间的关系，而非与GDP水平之间的关系，这样变暖对未来GDP就具有永久性影响。拟合得到的气温变化与经济影响分布，总体上得出的w*(τ)值低于2%，即使对于较小的τ也是如此，除非假定极端的参数值和/或气温分布发生了实质性移动。这些结果与温和的减排政策相一致。

title: Risk and Return in Environmental Economics
abstract: I examine the risk/return tradeoff for environmental investments, and its implications for policy choice. Consider a policy to reduce carbon emissions. To what extent does the value of such a policy depend on the expected future damages from global warming versus uncertainty over those damages, i.e., on the expected benefits from the policy versus their riskiness? And to what extent should the policy objective be a reduction in the expected temperature increase versus a reduction in risk? Using a simple model of a stock externality (e.g., temperature) that evolves stochastically, I examine the ``willingness to pay" (WTP) for alternative policies that would reduce the expected damages under ``business as usual" (BAU) versus the variance of those damages.I also show how one can compute ``iso-WTP" curves (social indifference curves) for combinations of risk and expected returns as policy objectives. Given cost estimates for reducing risk and increasing expected returns, one can compute the optimal risk-return mix for a policy, and the policy's social surplus.I illustrate these results by calibrating the model to data for global warming.
abstract_zh: 我考察了环境投资中的风险/收益权衡，及其对政策选择的含义。考虑一项减少碳排放的政策。该政策的价值在多大程度上取决于未来全球变暖的预期损害，还是取决于这些损害的不确定性，即取决于该政策的预期收益还是其风险性？政策目标在多大程度上应当是降低预期的气温升幅，而在多大程度上应当是降低风险？我运用一个关于随机演化存量外部性（例如气温）的简单模型，考察了为降低“照常排放”（BAU）情形下预期损害与降低损害方差而设计的各类替代政策的“支付意愿”（WTP）。我还展示了如何计算风险与预期收益组合的“等支付意愿”曲线（社会无差异曲线）以作为政策目标。给定降低风险和提高预期收益的成本估计，就可以计算政策的最优风险—收益组合，以及该政策的社会剩余。我通过将模型校准到全球变暖数据上来说明这些结果。

title: Fat Tails, Thin Tails, and Climate Change Policy
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy
abstract: Climate policy is complicated by the considerable compounded uncertainties over the costs and benefits of abatement. We don't even know the probability distributions for future temperatures and impacts, making cost-benefit analysis based on expected values challenging to say the least. There are good reasons to think that those probability distributions are fat-tailed, which implies that if social welfare is based on the expectation of a CRRA utility function, we should be willing to sacrifice close to 100% of GDP to reduce GHG emissions.I argue that unbounded marginal utility makes little sense, and once we put a bound on marginal utility, this implication of fat tails goes away: Expected marginal utility will be finite even if the distribution for outcomes is fat-tailed. Furthermore, depending on the bound on marginal utility, the index of risk aversion, and the damage function, a thin-tailed distribution can yield a higher expected marginal utility (and thus a greater willingness to pay for abatement) than a fat-tailed one.
abstract_zh: 气候政策因减排成本与收益中存在的大量叠加不确定性而变得复杂。我们甚至不知道未来气温及其影响的概率分布，这使得基于期望值的成本收益分析至少颇具挑战。有充分理由认为这些概率分布是厚尾的，这意味着：如果社会福利基于CRRA效用函数的期望值，我们就应当愿意牺牲接近100%的GDP来减少温室气体排放。我认为，无界的边际效用毫无道理，而一旦对边际效用设定上界，厚尾所隐含的这一结论就会消失：即使结果的分布是厚尾的，期望边际效用也将是有限的。此外，取决于边际效用的上界、风险厌恶指数和损害函数，薄尾分布所产生的期望边际效用（从而减排的支付意愿）可能高于厚尾分布。

title: Modeling the Impact of Warming in Climate Change Economics
venue: The Economics of Climate Change: Adaptations Past and Present
abstract: Any economic analysis of climate change policy requires some model that describes the impact of warming on future GDP and consumption. Most integrated assessment models (IAMs) relate temperature to the level of real GDP and consumption, but there are theoretical and empirical reasons to expect temperature to affect the growth rate rather than level of GDP. Does this distinction matter in terms of implications for policy? And how does the answer depend on the nature and extent of uncertainty over future temperature change and its impact? I address these questions by estimating the fraction of consumption society would be willing to sacrifice to limit future increases in temperature, using probability distributions for temperature and impact inferred from studies assembled by the IPCC, and comparing estimates based on a direct versus growth rate impact of temperature on GDP.
abstract_zh: 任何关于气候变化政策的经济分析，都需要某种描述变暖对未来GDP和消费影响的模型。大多数综合评估模型（IAM）将气温与实际GDP和消费的水平联系起来，但有理论和经验上的理由认为，气温影响的是GDP的增长率而非水平。这一区别在政策含义上是否重要？答案又如何取决于未来气温变化及其影响的不确定性的性质与程度？我通过以下方式来回答这些问题：利用IPCC汇编的研究所推断的气温和影响的概率分布，估计社会为限制未来气温上升而愿意牺牲的消费比例，并比较基于气温对GDP的直接影响与增长率影响的估计结果。

title: Solving Optimal Timing Problems in Environmental Economics
Governance, Issuance Restrictions, and Competition in Payment Card Networks
Sunk Costs and Risk-Based Barriers to Entry
Sunk Costs and Real Options in Antitrust
Mandatory Unbundling and Irreversible Investment in Telecom Networks
Uncertainty in Environmental Economics
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy
abstract: In a world of certainty, the design of environmental policy is relatively straightforward, and boils down to maximizing the present value of the flow of social benefits minus costs. But the real world is one of considerable uncertainty --over the physical and ecological impact of pollution, over the economic costs and benefits of reducing it, and over the discount rates that should be used to compute present values. The implications of uncertainty are complicated by the fact that most environmental policy problems involve highly nonlinear damage functions, important irreversibilities, and long time horizons. Correctly incorporating uncertainty in policy design is therefore one of the more interesting and important research areas in environmental economics. This paper offers no easy formulas or solutions for treating uncertainty --to my knowledge, none exist. Instead, I try to clarify the ways in which various kinds of uncertainties will affect optimal policy design, and summarize what we know and don't know about the problem.
abstract_zh: 在确定性的世界中，环境政策的设计相对直接，归结为最大化社会收益流的现值减去成本。但现实世界充满了相当大的不确定性——包括污染的物理与生态影响、减少污染的经济成本与收益，以及计算现值时应使用的贴现率。不确定性的影响之所以复杂，是因为大多数环境政策问题涉及高度非线性的损害函数、重要的不可逆性以及较长的时间跨度。在政策设计中正确纳入不确定性，因而是环境经济学中最有趣、最重要的研究领域之一。本文并不提供处理不确定性的简便公式或解决方案——据我所知，此类方案并不存在。相反，我试图厘清各类不确定性将如何影响最优政策设计，并总结我们对这一问题已知和未知的内容。

title: The Dynamics of Commodity Spot and Futures Markets: A Primer
Irreversibilities and the Timing of Environmental Policy
abstract: The standard framework in which economists evaluate environmental policies is cost-benefit analysis, so policy debates usually focus on the expected flows of costs and benefits, or on the choice of discount rate. But this can be misleading when there is uncertainty over future outcomes, when there are reversibilities, and when policy adoption can be delayed. This paper shows how two kinds of uncertainty over the future costs and benefits of reduced environmental degradation, and over the evolution of an ecosystem interact with two kinds of irreversibilities - sunk costs associated with an environmental regulation, and "sunk benefits" of avoided environmental degradation - to affect optimal policy timing and design.
abstract_zh: 经济学家评估环境政策的标准框架是成本收益分析，因此政策辩论通常聚焦于成本与收益的预期流量，或贴现率的选择。但当未来结果存在不确定性、存在不可逆性，且政策出台可以推迟时，这种做法可能会产生误导。本文展示了两类关于减少环境退化的未来成本与收益的不确定性，以及一个生态系统演化的不确定性，如何与两类不可逆性——与环境管制相关的沉没成本，以及避免环境退化所带来的“沉没收益”——相互作用，从而影响最优的政策时机与设计。

title: A Markup Interpretation of Optimal Investment Rules
The Long-Run Evolution of Energy Prices
abstract: In this paper I examine the long-run behavior of oil, coal, and natural gas prices, using up to 127 years of data, and address the following questions: Mat does over a century of data tell us about the stochastic dynamics of price evolution, and how it should be modelled? Can models of reversion to stochastically fluctuating trend lines help us forecast prices over horizons of 20 years or more? And what do the answers to these questions tell us about investment decisions that are dependent on prices and their stochastic evolution ?
abstract_zh: 本文考察了石油、煤炭和天然气价格的长期行为，利用了长达127年的数据，并讨论了以下问题：一个世纪的数据能告诉我们关于价格演变随机动态的哪些信息，以及应当如何对其建模？围绕随机波动的趋势线回归模型，能否帮助我们预测20年或更长时间跨度的价格？这些问题的答案又能告诉我们，哪些关于依赖价格及其随机演化的投资决策的信息？

Uncertainty in the Theory of Renewable Resource Markets
abstract: The natural growth rate of most renewable resource stocks is in part stochastic. This paper examines the implications of such ecological uncertainty for competitive equilibrium in a market with property rights. We show that stochastic fluctuations add a risk premium to the rate of return required to keep a unit of stock in situ, and we examine the effects of fluctuations on resource rent. Examples are used to show that extraction can increase, decrease, or be left unchanged as the variance of the fluctuations increases, depending on the extent of market “self-correction”. Regulatory implications are also discussed.
abstract_zh: 大多数可再生资源存量的自然增长率在一定程度上是随机的。本文考察了这种生态不确定性对具有产权市场中竞争性均衡的含义。我们表明，随机波动会在使单位存量保留于原地所需的收益率中增加一项风险溢价，并考察了波动对资源租金的影响。通过若干例子说明，取决于市场“自我修正”的程度，随着波动方差的增加，开采量可能增加、减少，也可能保持不变。文中还讨论了监管含义。

abstract: A rising world price of energy imposes a macroeconomic cost on the United States in two different ways. First, to the extent that energy is both an important input to production and a consumption good, with limited elasticities of substitution and demand, the economy's production and consumption possibilities are necessarily reduced as energy becomes more scarce. Work leading to this paper was supported by the Center for Energy Policy Research of the M.I.T. Energy Laboratory, and that support is gratefully acknowledged. abstract_zh: 世界能源价格的上涨以两种不同的方式对美国施加了宏观经济成本。第一，由于能源既是重要的生产投入品，又是消费品，而其替代弹性和需求弹性都有限，随着能源变得更为稀缺，经济的生产与消费可能性必然下降。因此，即使扩张性的货币与财政政策能够成功地将经济推向接近其充分产能的水平，所产生的实际国民收入也将低于能源价格未曾上涨时的水平。（本文早期版本曾于1979年11月9日在剑桥举办的CEPR能源价格、通货膨胀与经济活动会议上宣读。本文的研究工作得到了麻省理工学院能源实验室能源政策研究中心的支持，特此致谢。在撰写本文过程中，我从Olivier Blanchard、Stanley Fischer、Benjamin Friedman、Robert Hall、Franco Modigliani、Robert Solow以及一位匿名审稿人的交流与评论中受益良多。）
